detailed_rationale:
PNB Housing Finance has completed a genuine asset-quality turnaround: GNPA has fallen from a distressed 8.1% (Mar-2022) to 0.93% at FY26-end (Mar-2026), NNPA to 0.57%, and the retail-heavy book (99.5% of total loan assets, up from a legacy corporate/wholesale drag) grew loan assets to Rs 90,921 cr AUM (+13% YoY) with retail loans up 16% YoY to Rs 86,946 cr. FY26 consolidated PAT was Rs 2,291 cr (+18% YoY); Q4 FY26 PAT was Rs 655.8 cr (+19.2% YoY) on revenue of Rs 2,181.5 cr (+7.9%). ROA improved 10bps to 2.66% and ROE 54bps to 12.73%. CRAR remains very comfortable (~29-30% in the last reported quarter, Tier-I ~29%), so there is no capital constraint on the FY27 growth plan. [DATA, sourced Q4/FY26 press coverage].

One earnings-quality flag requires calling out explicitly: FY26 credit cost was NEGATIVE (-0.45%), driven by Rs 332 cr of recoveries on previously stressed/written-off accounts. That is a write-back, not a repeatable run-rate item, and it flatters the FY26 PAT growth print — normalized (positive) credit cost in FY27 is a headwind to earnings growth even if AUM grows at the guided 18-20% clip and pre-provision operating profit keeps pace. Management guidance for FY27: 18-20% loan growth, aiming to cross the Rs 1 lakh cr loan book, NIM held at 3.55-3.65% (helped by mix-shift to affordable/emerging segments and, more importantly, funding-cost relief from the CARE AAA/Stable long-term rating upgrade secured in May-2026 — CRISIL and ICRA still carry it AA+ as of their most recent (Oct-2025) actions, so a further multi-notch cost-of-funds benefit is not yet fully in hand across all rating agencies). The board approved (10-Jul-2026) a proposal to raise up to Rs 10,000 cr via NCDs (private placement, pending AGM shareholder approval) to fund the growth plan, alongside routine board strengthening (two new independent directors) and a Rs 8/share FY26 dividend (record date 31-Jul-2026, payout ratio only ~9% of EPS - retention-heavy, consistent with a growth-stage HFC).

On valuation: trailing PE ~12.4x, P/B ~1.5x (price ~Rs 1,090 vs book value ~Rs 738/share) against a trailing ROE of ~12.7%. A rough sustainable-growth check (ROE x retention ~12.7% x 0.91 payout-adjusted) lands close to 11-12%, broadly consistent with the current growth trajectory - i.e. the multiple is not obviously mispriced either way once the asset-quality repair is (largely) done and priced in via the rating upgrades. Screener's mechanical red flags ("low interest coverage," "poor 5y sales CAGR of 2.26%") are legacy artifacts of the pre-2023 corporate-book wind-down and the financial-sector interest-coverage exemption applies (leverage/interest expense is the business, not distress) - not fresh concerns. Separately, a Rs 237.43 cr fraud disclosure (M/s Sarv Realtors, reported to NHB/exchanges Jan-2026) relates to an account already fully written off in FY23 - a compliance-hygiene disclosure with no incremental P&L impact, not a new asset-quality event. Note: a secondary reference (Screener AI summary) to a larger, more recent "Happy Home Corporation" fraud (~Rs 421.81 cr, dated Jul-2026) could NOT be independently corroborated via web search/primary filings in this pass - flagging it as an unverified item for the desk to confirm directly against exchange filings before treating as a fact, per firm no-fabrication policy.
recommendation_rationale: Quant model scores this a Hold on both the 1y and 3y windows (54.9 / 55.8, mid-range - not borderline-Sell territory), and under the V1 asymmetric-override rule a Hold cannot be converted to a Sell by the analyst. Independently, the fundamental picture supports a Hold rather than an escalation to Sell: asset quality is genuinely repaired (not merely accounting-massaged) and rating agencies are validating it with upgrades, capital adequacy is ample, and the growth plan is credibly funded. The only meaningful drag is that FY26's negative credit cost is a one-off tailwind that will not repeat, so consensus PAT growth expectations built off the FY26 print need to be treated with some skepticism - a valuation/quality point, not a Sell-grade governance or asset-quality break.
summary: PNB Housing Finance has turned around its asset quality (GNPA down to sub-1% from over 8% four years ago) and is growing its retail book at a healthy mid-teens pace, funded comfortably by a strong capital base and a fresh AAA credit-rating upgrade. FY26 profit growth was flattered by one-off loan recoveries that will not repeat, so we would expect FY27 profit growth to run a bit below the 18-20% loan-book growth management is guiding to. At about 12-13x earnings and 1.5x book for a ~13% ROE lender, the stock looks fairly priced for what it is - a well-capitalized, much-improved but not exceptional-return housing financier - so we recommend holding rather than adding or exiting on fundamentals alone.
positive_para: The asset-quality turnaround is real and rating-agency-validated (GNPA 8.1% -> 0.93% over four years; CARE upgraded PNBHOUSING to AAA/Stable in May-2026), which lowers funding costs and de-risks the balance sheet at a business that is now 99.5% retail-loan-weighted. Capital adequacy (~29-30% CRAR) is well above regulatory minimums, giving multi-year runway to execute the 18-20% guided loan growth toward a Rs 1 lakh cr book without an equity raise. Promoter backing from Punjab National Bank remains intact and the company continues to strengthen its board and access debt markets on improving terms (Rs 10,000 cr NCD programme approved Jul-2026).
negative_para: FY26's headline profit growth (PAT +18%) is partly an artifact of a negative credit cost (-0.45%) driven by one-off recoveries (Rs 332 cr) that will not repeat; on a normalized credit-cost basis, FY27 earnings growth is likely to lag the guided AUM growth, which is a real risk to the growth number priced into consensus. ROE at ~12.7% is respectable but not exceptional for a name trading at ~1.5x book, so there is limited multiple re-rating room left purely from asset-quality repair - most of that re-rating has already happened. Two credit-rating agencies (CRISIL, ICRA) still carry only AA+ as of their latest actions, so the full funding-cost benefit of an AAA profile is not yet universally reflected; and a legacy fraud disclosure (Sarv Realtors, Rs 237 cr, already written off) plus an unverified secondary reference to a further, larger fraud disclosure both warrant the desk's ongoing disclosure-hygiene watch even though neither currently changes the P&L.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~12.4x trailing PE and ~1.5x P/B against a ~12.7% trailing ROE, the market is pricing in continued low-double-digit compounding (sustainable growth ~ ROE x retention ~= 11-12%, close to the 90%+ retention implied by the thin ~9% dividend payout) - i.e., roughly fair value for a repaired-but-not-exceptional-return HFC, not a distressed-multiple bargain nor a growth-stock premium. Because ROE sits at ~12-13% (not >=20%), this name does not qualify for the exceptional (>=25% growth) tier regardless of AUM guidance; growth here is credibly funded largely through retained earnings/debt rather than share dilution (no recent equity issuance), which is a genuine positive, but the multiple already reflects most of the asset-quality re-rating already delivered by the rating upgrades.
